title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
Embodied-Harness introduces a dual‑agent system that separates an Actor (environment interaction) from a Reflector (experience interpretation) via a Hierarchical Memory Architecture. This design enables recursive self‑improvement without changing model weights and yields 82.4‑94.4% success on RoboTwin2.0, RoboSPA and RMBench, and an average 96.7% success rate in real‑world trials.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no comparison to existing baselines, so the advantage of the dual‑agent framework is unclear.

## RoboTrack: Benchmark and data suite for point tracking in real-world robotic manipulation

### The Breakthrough
RoboTrack combines a 307‑clip human‑verified benchmark (2,522 tracks) with a 15 M synthetic point‑track dataset, boosting Average Jaccard scores by up to 5.1 points and enabling the RoboTracker‑Warp model to top four of five evaluated benchmarks; it is demonstrated guiding a pipette on a real robot.

### The Caveats
Real‑world validation is limited to a single pipette‑handling demo on one robot, with no quantitative evidence of higher manipulation success.

## Humanoid robots for safety‑critical electrical switching with a perception‑informed runtime safety filter

### The Breakthrough
The runtime filter fuses on‑board visual scene reconstruction with a target‑conditioned control‑barrier‑function QP, blocking unsafe commands while passing safe ones unchanged; it succeeded in all ten hardware trials on a Unitree G1 robot with zero unintended switch activations.

### The Caveats
The claim rests on only ten trials with a single robot and limited environmental variation, leaving robustness unproven.

## Waymo recalls robotaxis after they entered closed freeway lanes

### The Breakthrough
Waymo issued a voluntary recall to deploy software updates that improve navigation in closed freeway lanes and response to manual traffic‑control signals after robots entered restricted lanes.

### The Caveats
The recall is announced without independent testing, performance data, or baseline comparison, so the software improvements are unsubstantiated.

## Coprod raises $6M to launch modular robotics hardware stack

### The Breakthrough
Coprod’s “co:products” modular hardware stack couples interchangeable modules with a unified software API and a front‑end tool that auto‑generates datasheets and digital twins, claiming prototyping cycles shrink from two weeks to 24 hours and iteration cost drops to $5‑125 k.

### The Caveats
The claimed 24‑hour cycle and cost reduction are unverified, as no formal evaluation or baseline comparison is provided.

## Embo raises $110M seed to build general robotics brain with world models

### The Breakthrough
Embo proposes a single multimodal model pretrained from scratch on internet‑scale video, then fine‑tuned with robot experience and post‑trained via reinforcement learning, designed for high‑frequency motor control and dense video streams, and scales across 70,000 GPUs.

### The Caveats
The robot brain is announced without any hardware or simulation results, benchmarks, or baseline comparisons, leaving its claimed generality entirely unsubstantiated.

## Outcome Interfaces for Risk‑Aware Planning After Robot Damage

### The Breakthrough
Four model‑planner interfaces are evaluated, with a capability‑contract interface reducing declined missions from ~32% to 7‑8% for a Go2 quadruped and from ~57% to 35‑36% for an H1 humanoid under a 5% infeasibility limit.

### The Caveats
All results are confined to simulation, with no hardware experiments to confirm real‑world applicability.

## Task2Hand: A Contact‑Grounded Skill for Parametric Dexterous‑Hand Morphology Design

### The Breakthrough
Task2Hand’s cost‑ordered gating pipeline automatically generates and validates hand designs, producing the 4‑finger, 16‑DoF SAGE Hand that achieves 45.6% success on a hexagonal prism (vs 37.3% for LEAP) and 70.8% on a bicolor cylinder (vs 51.6% for LEAP), with dense tactile feedback halving drop rates.

### The Caveats
Improvements are demonstrated only in simulation on two objects, with no hardware experiments to confirm real‑world effectiveness.

## BEHAVIOR-1K: 1,000‑activity simulation benchmark for embodied AI

### The Breakthrough
The repository aggregates 1,000 everyday household activities derived from human time‑use surveys into a single simulation environment, offering consistent APIs and modular installation for embodied‑AI research.

### The Caveats
The benchmark provides no empirical results or baseline comparisons, so its comprehensiveness remains unvalidated.

## GTSAM: factor‑graph library for smoothing and mapping in robotics and vision

### The Breakthrough
GTSAM implements smoothing and mapping via factor‑graph formulation with optional CUDA linear solvers, Python toolbox and C++17 compatibility, enabling efficient batch and incremental optimization for SLAM, visual odometry, and sensor‑fusion pipelines.

### The Caveats
The claim of being a general‑purpose SAM framework is unsubstantiated without benchmark data or comparisons.

## Intel ros2_openvino_toolkit: OpenVINO integration for ROS 2 vision inference

### The Breakthrough
The toolkit wraps the OpenVINO runtime into ROS 2 nodes, supporting dozens of vision models and claiming up to ~19× speedup on Intel accelerators across ROS 2 Jazzy, Humble and Lyrical.

### The Caveats
The speedup claim lacks benchmark data, hardware tests, or comparisons to existing inference stacks.

### Priority
Embodied‑Harness showcases a concrete self‑improvement loop that delivers high success across multiple benchmarks and real‑world trials, making it the most actionable advance for manipulation today.

### One action
Consider prototyping a dual‑agent reflection loop in your own manipulation system to test whether experience‑driven guidance improves task success.
